body.en:
Such a large crowd gathered that Jesus got into a boat on the lake and taught from there, while everyone stood on the shore. He told a story: a farmer went out to sow seed. Some fell on the PATH, and birds ate it up.

Some fell on ROCKY ground, sprang up quickly, but withered fast because it had no root. Some fell among THORNS, which grew up and choked the plants.

But some fell on GOOD SOIL, came up, grew, and produced a crop — thirty, sixty, even a hundred times what was sown! Later, His disciples asked what it meant. Jesus explained: the seed is God's Word.

The path represents those who hear but Satan immediately snatches the message away. The rocky ground represents those who receive it with joy but fall away under any trouble, because they have no root. The thorny ground represents those choked by worries, wealth, and desires for other things.

But the good soil represents those who truly hear the word, accept it, and produce a remarkable harvest. Same seed, same Sower — but everything depends on the condition of the ground receiving it.

verse.en: Others, like seed sown on good soil, hear the word, accept it, and produce a crop.

title.en: A Song for Seeds on Different Ground

q.en: What happened to the seed that fell on the path?

en: It produced thirty times the crop

q.en: Why did the seed on rocky ground wither quickly, even though it sprang up fast?
What does the 'good soil' represent in Jesus' explanation?

en: People who never hear the word
Those who truly hear the word, accept it, and produce a crop

label.en: Activity sheet: Seeds on Different Ground

body.en:
Big idea: the condition of the heart determines the fruitfulness of God's Word in a life — the same message can be received with radically different outcomes depending on what's already growing (or not growing) within. This parable functions almost as an explanation for why people respond so differently to the very ministry Mark has been describing.

Conversation starters: (1) Which type of "soil" do you think best describes your heart right now? (2) What practical things choke spiritual growth like "thorns" — worries, busyness, wanting more stuff? (3) What helps "good soil" stay good — what keeps your heart receptive?

Pray for hearts that are good soil — receiving God's Word and producing real fruit.
